title: Embed+Rerank RPC facade: stable paging tokens, idempotent retries, and HTTP/gRPC error harmonization
creator: Arjun Mehta
description:
Summary: Build an RPC-style facade that provides stable iterator semantics for embeddings and rerank endpoints across legacy and new clients. The facade will normalize pagination tokens, provide idempotent retry semantics (retry hints and dedup keys), and harmonize HTTP error codes with existing gRPC/legacy clients to reduce client-side complexity.

Background: Multiple clients (legacy SDKs, new HTTP/REST, and internal gRPC routing) have diverging behaviors around cursor expiration, 429 vs 503 retryability, and partial failures when mixing embeddings and rerank calls in a pipeline. This causes customer-visible flakiness and broken migrations.

Goals:
- Define canonical pagination token format and TTL semantics that both legacy and new clients can consume.
- Implement server-side adapter that emits consistent error classes (retryable, throttled, fatal) mapped to existing HTTP codes and provides machine-consumable retry_hint fields.
- Ensure streaming and tool-calling flows that use embeddings+rerank chains gracefully fall back to best-effort results rather than hard failures.
- Provide migration playbook and SDK changes with compatibility flags.

Non-goals:
- Rewriting client SDKs in this ticket; SDK changes will be tracked separately.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Strong token immutability reduces server flexibility; we will version tokens so future behaviour can evolve.
- Adding dedup keys requires upstream clients to pass identifiers; for legacy clients we offer automatic hashing but with reduced guarantees.

Deliverables:
- API spec for facade and token format (Confluence link in attachments).
- Server adapter implementation behind feature flag + integration tests.
- Compatibility test matrix and a small canary rollout plan.
- Migration playbook for customers and SDK teams.
acceptance_criteria:
- Canonical pagination tokens documented and accepted by SDK owners.
- Requests using old cursor format are correctly translated and return the same results as before for 90% of test cases.
- Error responses include standardized 'error_type' and 'retry_after_ms' when applicable.
- Integration test demonstrating idempotent retry of embedding/rerank chain without duplicates.
- Canary run with two internal customers showing no increase in client-observed error rates.
